summary: Choose each episode boundary by looking at contact strips, then adversarially verify each choice

pick.ends_on: A young woman with her hair tied back, in a dark grey hoodie, stands behind a glass nursery window. She lifts her open palm to the glass and stares wide-eyed, lips parted in shock. Just before that, the white-haired grandfather in a dark suit leans in close over the bassinet.
pick.opens_on: The white-haired grandfather stands over a clear hospital bassinet holding a cane, with the swaddled baby in front of him. The caption reads "Investigate find the child's mother". The shot then cuts to the butler in a tuxedo and white gloves, writing in a small notebook.
pick.why: Neither option has any physical action near it. The last action ended about 4s before opt1 and the next one is about 13s after opt2, so the choice comes down to the hook. Opt2 lets the grandfather's claim ("looks exactly like Julian") finish inside the episode. It then ends on something new and unresolved: the mother pressed to the glass, shocked, watching strangers take her baby. That is a strong open question at a clean shot change. The next episode opens on a readable scene: an old man, a baby in a bassinet, and a butler taking notes. A cold viewer can tell who is who within a few seconds, and the first line ("find the child's mother") ties straight back to the woman we just saw. Lengths stay balanced: about 110s for this episode and about 96s for the next.
pick.rejected: Opt1 (424.433, the DP pick) ends on the grandfather leaning over the bassinet after "I'm taking you home", and the next episode opens on a close-up of the sleeping baby. That tension has already settled, since he has decided and nobody is pushing back. It also hands the mother's shocked reveal at the glass, the strongest hook in this stretch, to the next episode instead of ending on it.

verdict.reason: The cut at 433.1s holds up. I found no rule broken. index/scdet.txt puts a shot change exactly at 433.1: the Maggie-at-glass shot runs 431.77 to 433.1, and the frame at 433.1 is already the grandfather with his cane. The cut also falls in silence. Whisper has "baby" ending at 431.88 and "Investigate" starting at 433.46, so no line is split. Rule 2: there is no physical action at the cut. The hand going to the glass is a slow reaction gesture that is complete by about 432.5, and the nearest real action is the corridor run at about 446.6. Rule 3: the episode sets up the blood type, the 99.099% paternity result and "I'm taking you home". None of that has a physical payoff waiting just past 433.1. Rule 4: no impact is near. Rule 5: the next episode opens on the old man over a bassinet, the caption "Investigate find the child's mother" and the butler writing notes, which a cold viewer can read in a few seconds. The ending (a woman shocked at the nursery glass while he claims the baby) is an unresolved, fresh beat, so rule 6 is also met. Opt1 at 424.433 is also clean (shot change to the baby close-up, silence after "home" ends at 423.16), but it is only equal on rules 2-4, not strictly better. Its hook ("I'm taking you home") is weaker than adding the witness. Lengths check out: 109.7s and 95.8s, both inside the 95-150 band, though 95.8 is close to the floor. One factual correction to their description: the hoodie woman at the glass is NOT the mother. She is Maggie, the friend. At about 216s Layla (dark hair, striped gown, choker) tells her "Maggie please take the baby and go". Around 366s Maggie holds the S-monogram baby in the nursery. At 446-465s she runs to Layla's empty bed asking "Where did they take Leila". So their line that "find the child's mother" ties straight back to the woman we just saw is wrong. The mother is Layla, who has been taken away. This does not weaken the cut: the woman trusted to hide the baby watching the Sterlings claim him is at least as strong a hook. Their shot-level description is otherwise accurate: grandfather leaning in at 430.6-431.6, woman in grey hoodie, palm raised to the glass at 432.1-433.0, then grandfather with cane and the butler writing in a notebook.

pick.ends_on: A tight close-up of the dark-haired nanny with blue eyes, lips parted as she finishes her question (1912.1-1913.1). It then cuts to a wide shot of a dim hotel-style corridor: she stands on the left in a cream cable-knit cardigan, white top and black choker, looking up at a tall dark-haired man on the right in a navy suit and striped tie, who stares down at her without moving (1913.6-1914.1). No one has answered yet.
pick.opens_on: A new shot: a soft close-up of the same nanny against warm blurred background lights, her face turned slightly away with a worried look (1914.6). Over the next two seconds she lowers her gaze and closes her eyes, and her head drops a little (1915.1-1917.1), just before she admits "I did it". Her face fills the frame, so a cold viewer knows at once who is on screen.
pick.why: This is the only option the file offers. It passes the hard checks: strips_stale is false, the strip exists and opened, and I looked at every tile. The cut falls exactly on a clean shot change, from the wide two-shot to her close-up, so it is not inside any physical action. The scene is all talk: the flagged action is 102 s before and 8.9 s after, and nothing moves in these frames beyond her face. The episode ends on a strong open question. She has just asked whether what she did counts as leaking trade secrets, and the wide shot holds on him looming over her in silence, so the viewer wants to know whether he will fire her or worse. The tension is still live: her confession ("I did it"), her offer to leave and his decision to let it go once all come after the cut. The next episode opens on a close-up of the lead nanny, which a cold viewer can place within seconds. Her closing eyes lead straight into the confession, so continuous playback flows without a jump.
pick.rejected: There is no runner-up. The file has only one option (opt1, the dp pick), even though the task says to expect 2-8, so nothing could be compared. A cut anywhere later in this scene would come after her confession or his verdict, once the tension has resolved, which is weaker.

verdict.reason: I looked at every tile in review/frames/b1915_opt1.png. opt1 is the only option in the file, so no other option can beat it. The other reviewer's description matches the frames. From 1912.13 to 1913.13 there is a tight close-up of the blue-eyed nanny, lips parted, with the caption "That doesn't count as leaking trade secrets does it". The centre tile at 1914.63 is a new shot, a soft close-up of her in front of warm blurred lights, looking away with a worried face. Her eyes then close and her head lowers from 1915.13 to 1917.13. Checked against each rule. Rule 2: the cut falls exactly on a shot change and nobody moves except her face, so it is not inside a physical action. Rules 3 and 4: there is no impact or physical payoff nearby (the nearest flagged action is 102 s before and 8.9 s after), so no payoff is pushed into the next episode and no aftermath is cut short. Rules 5 and 6: the episode ends on her question with no answer yet, while he stands over her in silence. That question is still open, because her confession ("I did it"), her offer to leave and his decision to let it go all come after the cut. A cold viewer starts on a full-face close-up of the lead nanny, so they know who is on screen straight away, and her closing eyes lead straight into the confession, so continuous playback flows. I found no concrete fault.

pick.ends_on: A finger presses a lit button on a broadcast control desk. Then, one after another, the monitors on the control-room wall go black with "Signal lost". The episode ends on that wall, now almost all black "Signal lost" screens, with a single small monitor still showing the young woman in a cap holding up her papers to the camera. Two operators in headsets sit at the desk in front of it.
pick.opens_on: A warm lens flare washes over the dark monitor wall while the source's own "TO BE CONTINUED" card slides in down the right edge. The card holds over the dark wall for about 2 seconds. At about 4317.0 the picture cuts to a rainy parking lot seen from under a building's overhang: rain runs off the edge, and a black SUV is parked on the wet lot.
pick.why: The physical payoff here is the broadcast being killed. The button press is at about 4311.4, and the monitors switch to "Signal lost" from 4312.4 to 4314.5. Opt2 keeps the whole blackout inside this episode and gives it about 0.5-1 s of aftermath on the nearly black wall before the cut. The episode ends on a clear open question: who cut her feed, and what happens to her now? The cut falls just as the source's own end-of-episode transition (flare plus "TO BE CONTINUED") starts, so it matches where the drama itself meant to break. The next episode opens after the blackout, so nothing is split. Opt1 (the DP pick, 4313.4) cuts in the middle of the blackout: several monitors still show her live, and the rest go black in the first seconds of the next episode. That breaks the action in two and hands part of the payoff forward. Opt3 (4334.7) is flagged in_action: the cut lands on a page flip right before a pen crosses out "AVA", so it hands that beat to the next episode. It would also leave the "TO BE CONTINUED" card sitting in the middle of this episode, and the episode would end about 20 s after the signal-cut hook has already played out. Its next episode would open on a notebook close-up, where a cold viewer cannot tell who is on screen. One known flaw in opt2: the next episode opens on about 2 s of the leftover "TO BE CONTINUED" card before the parking-lot scene. No option cuts after the card, and opt1 carries the same card flaw plus the split blackout.
pick.rejected: Opt1 (the DP pick) cuts at 4313.4, halfway through the monitor blackout. Several screens still show the woman live, and the rest of the "Signal lost" blackout plus the "TO BE CONTINUED" card would open the next episode. The payoff is split and the card still leads off the next episode.

verdict.fault: Rules 3-4: the cut lands on the frame the blackout completes, with no aftermath, so the finished blackout and its hold go to the next episode, which also opens on the source's "TO BE CONTINUED" end card (against rule 1's no-card rule).
verdict.reason:
I pulled the source at 30 fps around the cut, cropped to the last live monitor (bottom-right, small). She is still live on it in every frame from 4314.600 through 4314.933. The first frame where it is dark is 4314.967, which is the chosen cut frame and also the frame where the flare and the "TO BE CONTINUED" card begin (scdet has a scene change at exactly 4314.966667). At 0.1 s steps, the upper screens are also still changing between 4314.6 and 4314.9, going from "Signal lost" text to fully black.

So opt2's last frame still shows her broadcasting. The blackout is not "kept whole inside this episode", and there is no "0.5-1 s of aftermath on the nearly black wall". The aftermath is about zero. The moment her last feed dies, plus the 2 s hold on the fully black wall, all open the next episode, under a leftover end card. That is the payoff-handoff and no-aftermath fault that rules 3 and 4 forbid, and an episode opening on "TO BE CONTINUED" goes against rule 1.

The description is also partly wrong. There are no operators in the final shot. The wide shot with the two operators in headsets ends at the 4313.4 shot change. From there to the cut, the framing is a closer view of the wall and desk with nobody in it.

The claim that "No option cuts after the card" holds only for the three listed options. index/candidates.json has a legal cut at 4316.967: the hard cut to the rainy parking lot, in_action false, 6.28 s clear of words before and 4.09 s after. Cutting there ends the episode on the fully black wall under the source's own "TO BE CONTINUED" card. That gives about 2 s of aftermath after the last screen dies, and it is exactly where the source itself broke. The next episode then opens straight on the parking lot. By about 4319 the woman in the blue striped shirt is on screen saying "Have you lost your mind Layla", and Layla herself (in the cap) appears by about 4323, well inside the 10 s rule. Episode lengths with the current neighbouring boundaries would be about 104.5 s and 119.8 s, both inside the band.

Among the listed options, opt2 is still the least bad. Opt1 (4313.4) cuts mid-blackout with several monitors still live. Opt3 (4334.7) is in_action on the page flip, and the pen crossing out "AVA" plays after the cut. So better_key is empty, but opt2 as chosen is flawed, and the boundary should move to 4316.967.

pick.ends_on: A tight close-up of the grey-haired woman (Helen, black high-neck blouse, dark red lipstick) in the dim hallway, with the dark-haired man's profile blurred at the left edge. She says "None of my concern" and her face settles into a slow, knowing half-smile.
pick.opens_on: A hard cut to a wide shot of the wood-panelled hallway. Helen, in a black suit with her silver hair in a bun, stands in front of a blonde woman in a burgundy satin robe. Within about 1.5s Julian comes into frame (dark hair, grey suit, gripping a carved wooden cane), and she turns on him with "The board cannot entrust a multi-billion dollar corporation...". Then comes an insert of his polished shoes and the cane tip on the red runner.
pick.why: The opt1 strip shows the break falling on a clean shot change. The episode closes on Helen's smug close-up, and the next opens on a wide shot of all three people. No physical action is under way: the nearest action is 15.8s away, and neither strip shows a blow or fall near the cut. The confrontation is also still unresolved at the cut. Her half-smile after "None of my concern" is an open question: what is she about to do to him? The very next line pays it off with the board threat. The wide opening frame helps a cold viewer. It sets up the stepmother, the blonde woman in the robe and Julian with his cane in one hallway within a couple of seconds, so everyone is placed well inside 10s. The physical beat before this, Julian throwing the coffee-bearing woman out around 4512-4518, finished long before the cut and stays in this episode.
pick.rejected: Opt2 (4572.067) is flagged in_action. Its centre tile is a blurred insert of a hand in the middle of snatching up the papers, so it cuts inside a motion. It also ends about 5s into a new, calm café scene: two young women at a round table reading documents after "Maggie help me investigate this". By then the hallway confrontation and the board threat are over, so the break falls after the tension has resolved. The next episode would then open on an out-of-focus close-up of a form rather than anyone's face, which is weak for a cold viewer.
